tasks.behavior: Support returns held money with one ops command that can't overpay or race a settlement
acceptance: cmd/ops case takes a pay link, receive address, payment transaction or invoice id and prints each held payment: sender, amount, why it is held, what is refundable now and when all of it is. Backend only, no UI.

ops return checks the payment is final and reached this receiver, caps the amount at what is both held and refundable and at least 0.10 USD (D-90), refuses a zero, receiver, token, factory or invoice-address destination, warns for a contract or an address that didn't pay, and dry-runs the transfer and the refund.

It sets refund_pending before it prints the calls (the receiver's deploy when needed, then refund), one return per option at a time, and not while any movement is unbooked. Process keeps refund_pending until a refund is booked; reopen refuses it; the watcher keeps reading the receiver past its window; the attention list keeps it. ops release unlocks a return that won't be sent.

The watcher books the return once, refund_pending becomes held or refunded, and the owner's payment page shows it: a Returned to the payer row in Transfers, the timeline's last step, and no extra held any more.
No new key: the command reads and prints; its only write is the refund status and its history row.
notes: 2026-10-31 review fail by reviewer: FAIL, one money defect. The tool can send the creator's money when the ledger is behind the chain. returns.go:236 caps a return at min(ledger held, on-chain refundable). Past an unsettled deadline (factory paused or signer down longer than the grace, a case operations.md expects), refundable is the whole balance, so the ledger is the only guard for the creator's share. That guard is stale while a sent refund is not booked yet. Reproduced on Anvil with a temporary overlay test (removed afterwards): 5 USDC invoice paid 6, never settled, past the deadline; ops return, Safe sends it, ops release before the watcher books it, ops return again. Both dry runs pass, a second 1 USDC goes out, the receiver keeps 4 of the 5 owed, and the outflow books as refund_consumed_payable. A refund sent outside the tool opens the same gap with no release at all. Under D-60 the person who releases is not the one who signed in the Safe, so this mix-up is plausible. Fix: QueueReturn refuses while the receiver's chain balance (h.Balance) is below the ledger's receiver balance (ledger.ReadAmounts already gives Receiver): money has left and isn't booked yet. Add a test like the one above. money-safety.md:93 should also say: reject the Safe transaction and check it was not executed before you release. Fine as written: two operators at once (the conditional UPDATE at returns.go:315 lets one win, and the other gets ErrReturnQueued before anything prints). Return during a settlement (refundable before the deadline is balance minus amount; Process keeps refund_pending). Reopen refuses refund_pending (invoice/reopen.go:66, get.go:185). The status decode of words 5 and 8 matches InvoiceStatus. The printed Data equals cast calldata of the printed signature and args (checked), the cast form runs in the tests, the arguments are only hex and digits so the quoting is safe, and the Transaction Builder custom data step is right. Lookup: pay_token is unique, lowercase and only on main rows. An invoice id is read as a tx hash and finds nothing, never the wrong invoice. No secret is printed: errors go through chain.Redact, and with-env.sh drops the keys. All three fixes fail without their change (Process, watcher holding, attention list: checked with go -overlay). The targeted tests, go test ./cmd/ops and go vet pass, and ops case ran read-only on a local Tempo invoice. Non-blocking: (1) main.go:103 needs -tx to touch exactly one invoice, so a 4337 bundle or a batch that pays two invoices can't be returned, and the error says not a final payment. (2) With several payers, -amount is capped only by the option's total held, so support works out each payer's share by hand. (3) Another invoice's receive address is not refused as a destination (returns.go:233). It only gets the warning that no payment came from it. (4) money-safety.md:77 says -to warns, but the warning is for a destination that made no payment. (5) No tests cover ErrAmountNeeded, a token or factory destination, the contract warning, or main.go picking the option. (6) returns.go:33 repeats the deploy signature from contract.go:19. returns.go:196 prints <nil> on a short reply. ErrNotYet names the deadline even after it has passed. (7) The pay copy warns only about under 0.10 USD, but D-90 says Need help also warns that unclaimed money may never come back. (8) operations.md:32 says check receiverOf(invoiceId), which can't pass before the deploy in a batch. (9) with-env.sh keeps CANARY_RPC_URLS for ops.

2026-10-31 review pass by reviewer: PASS after 941492b6. The defect is fixed. QueueReturn now refuses with ErrUnbooked while the receiver's chain balance is below the ledger's receiver balance (returns.go:219). TestSupportWaitsForASentRefundToBeBookedBeforeTheNextReturn is the reproduced scenario. With the guard removed through go -overlay, it fails ('a second return before the first was booked: <nil>'). As committed, it passes. I tried to break the guard. (a) An unbooked late deposit can hide an unbooked refund. Reproduced: return, send, release, then a 1 USDC deposit from another address, not yet scanned; the second return is accepted. The creator stays whole: the receiver keeps 5 of 5, payable is 5, held is 0, no policy exception. The guard passes only when unbooked money in is at least unbooked money out, so the old held figure never exceeds what will be held once both are booked. The late payer's 1 USDC still went to the first payer. The creator could lose only if that deposit were later reorged away and the Safe's refund was mined again. Non-blocking: refusing while any deposit to the option is detected and not booked would close this too. (b) Arc: a native top-up to an undeployed receive address that no Transfer log records would hide it the same way. The creator's amount stays on chain, and the ledger flags it (refund_consumed_payable plus the balance alert). The 6-decimal balanceOf rounds down, so it never trips the guard by mistake. (c) A settlement on its way, a lagging RPC or an unreadable token make it refuse for now, which is safe; the error names the cause. The other fixes check out. main.go picks this case's option out of a transaction that pays several invoices. Any invoice's receive address is refused, with tests for the token, the factory, another receiver and the contract warning. There is one deploy signature constant, a short reply reports its length, and ErrNotYet names the deadline only while it is ahead. tasks.behavior: Payments confirm and settle without waiting for unrelated offered networks
acceptance: Reproduce: a payment final on its own network stays unbooked while another offered network lags. Keep a regression test.
The first payment final on its own network chooses its option, is booked and queued to settle at once; no other offered network is waited for.

notes: 2026-10-30 Owner request: investigate and fix cross-network waiting, then let the implementing agent merge. This task records findings only; no implementation is started.

2026-10-30 Root cause: internal/ledger/process.go:100-126 refuses to choose an option until every other enabled option chain has last_finalized_time greater than the deposit block_time. It returns before booking; settlement_intents are created only after paid at lines 336-343. The slowest offered network therefore delays faster ones.

2026-10-30 Current policy deliberately chooses the earliest payment across chains (R-119/D-76), protecting an earlier full payment from later dust. This is a policy change, not permission to delete the guard or replace finalized evidence with latest blocks. Preserve the safety purpose through an explicit attempt-selection design.

2026-10-30 internal/invoice/pick.go:16-18 currently treats the payer pick as display preference, not binding payment selection. internal/invoice/payments.go:61 labels detected as Confirming even when the deposit itself is confirmed and only cross-network selection is waiting.

tasks.behavior: Protected changes, like making an API key, confirm the user in one clear step that fits the app, or not at all when research shows the check isn't needed
acceptance: Research how Stripe, GitHub, Vercel, Coinbase, Cloudflare and Linear confirm sensitive actions: what they protect, what proof they ask for, how long it lasts, and how it looks. Notes in docs/research with sources.

Decide, for each action D-63 lists (API keys, webhook secrets, team roles, billing details, money actions), whether it needs a fresh sign-in and what proves it. Update D-63, R-144, R-146 and the code together, and say why.
No dialog opens on top of another dialog: the confirmation happens in place, and the user still sees what they confirm.
The proof is the easiest the user has (a passkey before an email code), and one confirmation covers the next protected changes for the whole window.
The code input in the confirmation looks and behaves like the kit's CodeInput on the sign-in page; find why it differs in the dialog and fix it there.
Every place that asks for a fresh sign-in (api-keys, team, webhooks, billing, money actions) uses the new flow, and browser tests cover it, including a wrong and an expired code.
